summary: SPACE LEGACY is an interactive 3D web-based virtual space museum built with Three.js and WebGL that brings humanity's off-world exploration history to life. Users can navigate a real-time, procedurally textured solar system, fly between planets and the Moon via cinematic orbital transitions, and inspect glowing surface hotspots representing real space artifacts—such as rovers, landers, telescopes, and deep-space probes—complete with telemetry data, surface captures, and archival records.   Space exploration archives are often scattered across dense technical databases that feel inaccessible to general audiences and non-English speakers. SPACE LEGACY addresses this challenge by combining spatial 3D visualization with an age-adaptive content engine that tailors mission summaries for children, teens, and adults, alongside a real-time multilingual engine supporting over 75 languages with full right-to-left (RTL) layout adaptation and offline telemetry simulation.   By transforming complex NSSDCA mission records into an intuitive, inclusive experience, SPACE LEGACY democratizes space education and inspires future explorers worldwide.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works: SPACE LEGACY is an interactive 3D web-based virtual space museum that transforms the solar system into a living, explorable digital archive of human space exploration. Upon entering, users input their age and select their preferred language. They can then navigate a real-time 3D solar system, click on any planet or Earth's Moon to trigger smooth orbital camera transitions, rotate celestial bodies in 360 degrees, and select glowing surface hotspots mapped to real planetary coordinates. Each hotspot opens an interactive mission dossier displaying historical summaries, NASA/NSSDCA telemetry data, surface captures, and a live simulated radar/telemetry reel.

2. Benefits:

  • Personalized Learning: Dynamically adapts mission explanations into three distinct reading levels—Child (≤12), Teen (13–18), and Adult (19+)—so learners of all ages grasp complex aerospace concepts effortlessly.
  • Universal Accessibility: Supports over 75 world languages with real-time asynchronous translation, local storage caching, and full Right-to-Left (RTL) layout adaptation.
  • Fast, Lightweight Performance: Generates planetary textures, bump maps, and atmospheric shaders procedurally in code, eliminating heavy 3D asset downloads.

3. Intended Impact: SPACE LEGACY aims to democratize space education and preserve humanity's off-world heritage. By turning dense technical mission records into an intuitive, story-driven visual experience, the project bridges the gap between scientific archives and the general public—inspiring students, educators, and space enthusiasts worldwide regardless of age, language, or technical background.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used:

  • Coding Languages: JavaScript (ES6+ Modules), HTML5, CSS3, and GLSL (OpenGL Shading Language for custom Sun plasma, starfield twinkle, and Fresnel atmospheric glow shaders).
  • Libraries & APIs: Three.js (v0.171.0) & WebGL for 3D rendering, HTML5 Canvas 2D API for procedural textures and offline radar simulation, Fetch API for dynamic translation, and Web Storage API (localStorage) for caching translations and preferences.
  • Data & Hardware: Mission records and coordinates curated from NASA and NSSDCA (NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive) catalogs. Runs directly in any modern WebGL-capable desktop or mobile browser without specialized hardware.

5. How the Project Is Creative: Instead of relying on static text pages or heavy pre-rendered 3D models, SPACE LEGACY combines procedural planetary art (generating continents, craters, cloud layers, and Saturn's Cassini division rings mathematically) with a 100% offline HTML5 Canvas telemetry feed simulatorand cinematic quadratic Bezier warp-speed transitions. Pairing real NSSDCA coordinates with age-tailored storytelling turns raw space data into an immersive museum beyond Earth.

6. Key Factors Considered:

  • Inclusivity & Localization: Engineered automatic typography switching (Cairo and Manrope fonts) and mirrored UI layouts for RTL languages like Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, and Urdu.
  • Accessibility & Motion Sensitivity: Added prefers-reduced-motion detection to shorten warp animations for motion-sensitive users, along with full keyboard (Escape key) and ARIA screen-reader support.
  • Offline Resilience & Responsiveness: Built fallback image handling, local translation caching, and responsive mobile-to-desktop layouts so the museum remains functional across varying network conditions and screen sizes.
